rows.surface: Account/license provenance and private backup authorization
rows.mechanism: Capture immutable upload license and authoritative app from the registered profile; revalidate owner, token, activation binding and license. Legacy records retain origin-only access. Web owner management stays account-scoped. The native window root is now a key-only activation screen until a fresh valid daemon publication unlocks it. Revocation/expiry/malformed/stale publication replaces the entire workspace and presented sheets, with an opaque background cover and foreground recheck. Existing signing keys and license authority remain unchanged; UI state alone does not authorize daemon operations. On 2026-09-23 the public web workspace and installation pages were retired in favor of a private admin-only console; device APIs, stored backups and their authorization were preserved. The source-built launcher/daemon/tweak path uses its existing native RS256 verifier and SocialBox deployment, independently of the recovered engine. Fresh installs select that origin; malformed explicit origins fail closed. First-activation rejection remains visible without a pairing. The source daemon also gates queued mutations and direct clone provisioning before any profile access or dispatch. Locked refresh publishes only local state; activation, traffic closure and diagnostic recovery remain available.

rows.surface: Private owner admin console, session routing and license-key presentation
rows.mechanism: The owner console and sign-in remain private; /install is a public client entry page exposing only public release status and support links. Signed claims prefilter the canonical configured seed email and admin role; the server layout and every admin API re-read the stored identity and role. Dedicated same-origin owner login issues only an owner session. Customer native login/registration, license/device APIs, backups, existing signer, passwords, session cookie and both old APT repositories retain their contracts. Plaintext generated keys remain in component memory and require acknowledgement. Release UI and /updates remain dormant redirects; /install offers only a promoted upgrade when available, never a fresh-install package or unapproved download. The machine update API remains available. License generation/edit/enable/delete/revoke additionally recheck one unique current actor under the same auth-state transaction callback, before effects. HTTP revoke uses a required-actor API; typed denial does not publish or append audit. Private license/user read endpoints also require that unique current owner in the final auth snapshot used for synchronous projection. Separate audit read precedes the final license guard; user rows and device counts share that same auth snapshot. No authorization write transaction or storage migration contract change. Owner-requested new device issuance fixes expiresAt:null/maxActivations:1 and refuses duration/expanded-limit inputs before issuance; form removes those choices. Existing rows/bindings/history and native freshness/deadlines are unchanged. One installation/bearer is not hardware attestation; local tests/build/browser acceptance is not production or customer/runtime acceptance.
